title: Nothing Compares 2 U
trivia: Prince wrote it for his side project The Family, but O'Connor's stark reading made it a worldwide number one. The video, a near-unbroken close-up of her face with a single tear, became as famous as the song.

track.title: Nothing Compares 2 U
track.album: I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got
track.notes: O'Connor 1990 version, not The Family or Prince.

notes: Cover of The Family (1985, written by Prince), but O'Connor's is the famous recording. Single Jan 1990, album Mar 1990.

title: Ice Ice Baby
trivia: It borrows its bass riff from a Queen and David Bowie single, and it was the first hip-hop single to top the US Hot 100.

track.title: Ice Ice Baby
track.notes: SBK 1990 To the Extreme version, not the 1989 Ichiban version.

notes: An earlier 1989 Ichiban version was a B-side and was partly re-recorded for the SBK release; the 1990 SBK recording is the hit and the card year. Single Aug 1990, album Sept 1990.

title: No Son of Mine
trivia: It tells of a son estranged from his father and was the lead single from We Can't Dance. At more than six minutes it is one of the longer hits the band ever had.
notes: Single and album both Nov 1991. Single edit is shorter than the album cut.

title: Smells Like Teen Spirit
trivia: The title came from a deodorant brand that a friend had scrawled on Kurt Cobain's wall, a product he did not know existed. The song pulled grunge out of Seattle and into the mainstream.
notes: Single Sept 1991, album Nevermind Sept 1991.

title: Alive
trivia: Eddie Vedder wrote the lyrics over an instrumental demo by guitarist Stone Gossard. Vedder has said the story was loosely drawn from his own family history.
notes: Album Aug 1991, single followed (promo Jul 1991).

title: Under the Bridge
trivia: Anthony Kiedis wrote it as a poem about loneliness and addiction, and producer Rick Rubin talked him into showing it to the band. It was a softer turn for a group known for funk-rock energy.
notes: Album Sept 1991, single Mar 1992. Hitster NL also lists 1991.

title: All That She Wants
trivia: The Swedish group built its sound on a reggae-tinged pop lilt, and this was the breakout. The lyrics are about a woman who wants a baby and then moves on.
notes: Album Happy Nation (Europe) is the same material as the US album The Sign. First released late 1992 in Scandinavia.

title: Why
trivia: Lennox's first solo single after the end of Eurythmics. It opened her debut album Diva, which went straight to number one in the UK.
notes: Single Feb 1992, album Apr 1992.

title: Sing Hallelujah!
trivia: Nigerian-born Swedish artist Alban Nwapa really is a trained dentist, which is where the stage name comes from. The song became a big dance hit across Europe.
notes: Album One Love Nov 1992 includes the track; the single came Feb 1993 and charted in 1993 (Hitster NL shows 1993). Card follows the strict first-release rule and uses 1992. Hitster NL list shows 1993; card uses 1992.

title: Everybody Hurts
trivia: Drummer Bill Berry came up with the music and Michael Stipe wrote the words with teenagers in mind. The strings were arranged by John Paul Jones of Led Zeppelin.
notes: Album Oct 1992, single Mar 1993. Album-first year.

title: Creep
trivia: The loud guitar crunches before the chorus were Jonny Greenwood's attempt to spoil a song he did not like, and they became its hook. The band later grew weary of being known for it.
notes: Single Sept 1992 (a hit only on re-release in 1993), album Feb 1993. Album-first/single-first year 1992. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: Informer
trivia: The Toronto artist rapped in a Jamaican-flavoured style, and it spent seven weeks at number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 in early 1993.
notes: Single Aug 1992 (Canada), album Jan 1993; US chart peak came in 1993. Year follows first release.

title: The Rhythm of the Night
trivia: Brazilian-born singer Olga Souza fronted this Italian dance project. It broke through in Europe first and only reached the US charts well over a year later.
notes: Italian single Nov 1993, international 1994, album Apr 1995.

title: Mr. Vain
trivia: The song is a swipe at a conceited man, and it climbed to number one in Germany, the UK and many other countries in 1993. Tania Evans sings the hook against Jay Supreme's rap.

track.title: Mr. Vain
track.notes: Radio edit about 3:54; album mix longer.

notes: Single Apr 1993 (Dance Pool), album Serenity 1993.

title: What Is Love
trivia: The Trinidad-born, German-based singer found a second life for the track when it became the head-bobbing soundtrack of a 1998 comedy film.
notes: Wikipedia gives single 18 Jan 1993; Discogs lists a German CD maxi dated Dec 1992. Card uses 1993 (the widely cited release, matches Hitster).

artist: Reel 2 Real feat. The Mad Stuntman
title: I Like to Move It
trivia: Erick Morillo produced it with The Mad Stuntman on the mic. The song got a second life when a singing lemur performed it in the 2005 animated film Madagascar.

track.artist: Reel 2 Real feat. The Mad Stuntman
track.title: I Like to Move It

notes: Single Oct 1993 (Strictly Rhythm), album Move It! Oct 1994.

title: Cotton Eye Joe
trivia: The folk song Cotton-Eye Joe is older than the American Civil War. Swedish group Rednex gave it a fast dance makeover with banjo and fiddle samples.
notes: Arrangement of a traditional folk song; Rednex's is the famous recording. Single 1994, album Sex and Violins 1995.

title: Zombie
trivia: Dolores O'Riordan wrote it as a protest after an IRA bomb in Warrington, England, killed two children in 1993. The distorted guitar and her keening vocal made it the band's best-known song.
notes: Single Sept 1994, album Oct 1994.

title: Self Esteem
trivia: The narrator knows he is being walked all over and does nothing about it. The album Smash became one of the best-selling independent-label albums ever.
notes: Album Apr 1994, single followed.

title: Waterfalls
trivia: Organized Noize wrote and produced it, and Left Eye added her own rap verse. The lyrics deal with drug dealing and HIV/AIDS, unusual subjects for a pop hit.
notes: Album CrazySexyCool Nov 1994, single May 1995. Album-first year; Hitster NL lists 1995. Hitster NL list shows 1995; card uses 1994.

title: Love Is All Around
trivia: The Scottish band's version of a 1967 hit spent fifteen weeks at number one in the UK, one of the longest runs ever. It came from the soundtrack of a romantic comedy.

track.title: Love Is All Around
track.notes: Wet Wet Wet 1994 version, not The Troggs.

notes: Cover of The Troggs (1967), but Wet Wet Wet's is the famous recording. Single May 1994.

title: Ironic
trivia: The lyrics list a run of unlucky situations, and listeners have argued ever since about whether any of them are actually ironic.
notes: Album Jun 1995, single early 1996. Album-first year. Not on the Hitster NL list; seen on the Hitster Canada edition list.

title: Captain Jack
trivia: A marching, military-flavoured dance track that was the debut single of the German act of the same name. It reached the UK top ten on re-release in 1996.
notes: Hitster NL lists 1995. Radio mix ~3:30. First released 1995 in Germany.

title: Gangsta's Paradise
trivia: The track is built on Stevie Wonder's Pastime Paradise. Wonder reportedly agreed to the sample on condition that the lyrics stay free of profanity.
notes: Single Aug 1995 (from Dangerous Minds soundtrack), album Nov 1995.

title: Don't Speak
trivia: Gwen Stefani wrote it with her brother Eric about the end of her relationship with bandmate Tony Kanal. It was a ballad from a band known for ska energy.
notes: Album Oct 1995, single Apr 1996. Album-first year; Hitster NL lists 1996. Hitster NL list shows 1996; card uses 1995.

title: Wonderwall
trivia: Noel Gallagher has said it is about an imaginary friend who will save you from yourself, though most listeners took it as a love song.
notes: Album Oct 2 1995, single Oct 30 1995. Album-first year (same year either way).

title: I Wanna Be a Hippy
trivia: The vocal hook was lifted from a David Peel song about marijuana and put over fast hardcore techno. It topped the charts in several European countries.

track.title: I Wanna Be a Hippy
track.notes: Original or Flamman and Abraxas radio mix.

notes: English duo (Greater Than One) on the Dutch label Mokum. Debut as B-side of Mary Jane EP, lead single Jun 1995. Best-known release is the Flamman and Abraxas radio mix.

title: Più bella cosa
trivia: The title means the most beautiful thing. It was a big hit across continental Europe for one of Italy's best-selling singers.
notes: Single and album both 1996; exact order not verified.

title: Return of the Mack
trivia: A UK number one in April 1996. The title uses mack, slang for a smooth-talking ladies' man, and the lyrics are about coming back after a break-up.
notes: Single Mar 1996 (WEA), album Apr 1996.

title: Wannabe
trivia: It reached number one in more than 30 countries and made the Spice Girls a global phenomenon. The spoken-word rap in the middle is one of pop's best-known bridges.
notes: Single Jul 1996 (UK), album Nov 1996. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: Barbie Girl
trivia: Barbie's maker Mattel sued the group's label, and the appeals judge ended his ruling by advising both sides to chill.
notes: Album Mar 1997, single May 1997. Danish-Norwegian group.

title: My Heart Will Go On
trivia: James Horner wrote the music for the film Titanic, and Dion was reportedly reluctant at first to record a pop song for it. The song won the Oscar for Best Original Song.
notes: Appears on both Let's Talk About Love and the Titanic soundtrack (both Nov 1997). Single Dec 1997.

title: Tubthumping
trivia: The Leeds band began as anarchist punks. At the 1998 Brit Awards, a member poured water over the deputy prime minister on stage.
notes: Often listed as Tubthumping (I Get Knocked Down). Album and single Aug 1997.

title: Save Tonight
trivia: Cherry is the son of jazz trumpeter Don Cherry and the half-brother of Neneh Cherry. The song was an international hit in 1998.
notes: Swedish release 1997; the international rollout and chart peaks came in 1998. Card uses first-release year 1997 (matches Hitster).

title: Torn
trivia: The Australian singer and former soap actress topped the charts across much of the world with it, and it became the biggest hit of her career.
notes: Cover of Ednaswap (1995) and Lis Soerensen (1993), but Imbruglia's is the famous recording. Single Sept 1997, album Nov 1997.

title: Stop
trivia: The track has a Motown-flavoured bounce that nods to 1960s girl groups. It came from the group's second album.
notes: Album Spiceworld Nov 1997, single Feb 1998. Album-first year; Hitster NL lists 1998. Hitster NL list shows 1998; card uses 1997.

title: Bitter Sweet Symphony
trivia: A legal fight over the string sample, taken from an orchestral version of a Rolling Stones song, cost the band the royalties until Jagger and Richards gave up their share in 2019.
notes: Single Jun 1997, album Sept 1997.

title: Gettin' Jiggy wit It
trivia: Built on a sample of Sister Sledge's He's the Greatest Dancer, it won Smith the Grammy for Best Rap Solo Performance.
notes: Album Nov 25 1997, single Jan 1998. Album-first year; Hitster NL lists 1998. Hitster NL list shows 1998; card uses 1997.

title: ...Baby One More Time
trivia: Swedish songwriter Max Martin wrote it, and it reached number one in more than 20 countries.
notes: Single 23 Oct 1998, album Jan 1999. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: Believe
trivia: The producers long said the warped vocal was a vocoder, but it was actually pitch-correction software pushed to an extreme. The effect was soon nicknamed after the singer.
notes: Single Oct 1998, album Nov 1998. Not on the Hitster NL list; seen on the Hitster Germany edition list.

title: Blue (Da Ba Dee)
trivia: The lyrics describe a character whose whole world is blue, and the hook is mostly nonsense syllables. The Italian trio turned it into a global hit in 1999.
notes: Italian single Oct 1998 (Skooby), album Europop Nov 1999. Sources vary on the month, not the year. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: God Is a DJ
trivia: The title treats club culture as a kind of church, and Maxi Jazz's low, spoken delivery became the band's signature.
notes: Album Sunday 8PM and single both 1998.

title: Praise You
trivia: It samples a spoken-word track by Camille Yarbrough. The video was shot without permission outside a cinema, with director Spike Jonze posing as the leader of a fake dance troupe.

track.title: Praise You
track.album: You've Come a Long Way, Baby

notes: Album Oct 1998, UK single Jan 1999. Album-first year.

title: Fly Away
trivia: It earned Kravitz the first of four consecutive Grammys for Best Male Rock Vocal Performance. Its soaring chorus made it one of his most recognised songs.
notes: Album 5 May 1998; single followed in late 1998 or early 1999. Album-first year.

title: I Want It That Way
trivia: Max Martin and Andreas Carlsson wrote it in Sweden. Critics and fans have long debated what its lyrics are actually saying.
notes: Single Apr 1999, album May 1999. Not on the Hitster NL list; seen on the Hitster Canada edition list.

title: Genie in a Bottle
trivia: Her debut single, it spent five weeks at number one in the US in 1999.
notes: Single Jun 1999, album Aug 1999.

title: If You Had My Love
trivia: Her debut single came before an album named after the New York subway line she rode from the Bronx to Manhattan.
notes: Single May 1999, album Jun 1999.

title: Mambo No. 5 (A Little Bit of...)
trivia: The German singer added a list of girls' names to Dámaso Pérez Prado's 1949 mambo instrumental. The result became a summer 1999 smash across Europe.

track.title: Mambo No. 5 (A Little Bit of...)
track.notes: Lou Bega 1999 version, not Perez Prado.

notes: Reworking of Perez Prado (1949); Bega's version is the famous recording. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: Porcelain
trivia: Nearly every track on the album Play was licensed for film, TV or advertising, which helped it become a worldwide hit.
notes: Album 17 May 1999, single Jan 2000. Album-first year.
